comparisons.peer_topic: Data center and cloud computing solutions
comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers a deep portfolio of data center solutions including AI accelerators, CPUs, GPUs, DPUs, SmartNICs, and FPGAs to meet performance requirements for data centers, supercomputers, and cloud environments.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and AMD disclose their respective data center and cloud infrastructure solutions aimed at meeting the performance requirements of modern computing environments. AVGO focuses on its infrastructure software value proposition, offering customers 'choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.' In contrast, AMD describes its hardware portfolio, offering 'AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs)' to meet the 'vast computing performance requirements' of similar data center and cloud environments.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.

We offer a deep portfolio of data center computing solutions including AI accelerators, microprocessors (CPUs), graphic processing units (GPUs), data processing units (DPUs), Smart Network Interface Cards (SmartNICs), and field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs), to meet the vast computing performance requirements of today's data centers, supercomputers, AI and Machine Learning (ML) data center environments and cloud environments.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel launched Intel Xeon 6 processors for data centers using Intel 3 process and Efficient cores, designed to address diverse workload deployments. The 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, continued to ramp throughout 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify data center CPU advancements as key components of their infrastructure strategy. AVGO describes its infrastructure software solutions designed to support applications across various cloud environments, implicitly relying on underlying compute infrastructure. INTC explicitly details its data center CPU product launches, stating that the 'Intel Xeon 6 family is designed to address the growing diversity in workloads and deployments in the data center environments,' mirroring the broad infrastructure utility described by AVGO.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.

▪Data center CPUs. We launched our Intel® Xeon® 6 processors for the data center, utilizing the Intel 3 process, including our first Intel Xeon processor using Efficient cores (E-cores). The Intel Xeon 6 family is designed to address the growing diversity in workloads and deployments in the data center environments. Our 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, based on Intel 7, were launched in 2023, and continued to ramp throughout 2024.

comparisons.peer_summary: CNBU data center sales were driven by server demand in cloud and enterprise markets, with growth fueled by the shift of infrastructure and workloads to the cloud and the memory-intensive nature of AI data-centric workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and MU discuss the drivers of data center market growth, specifically linking them to cloud infrastructure and AI workloads. AVGO's software solutions enable customers to 'connect and protect applications and data at scale,' supporting the broader cloud ecosystem. MU explicitly states that 'data center sales were driven primarily by server demand across the cloud and enterprise markets' and that 'cloud-native workloads are drivers of growth,' highlighting the shared dependency on cloud and enterprise data center expansion.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.
Data center: CNBU sales to the data center end market were driven primarily by server demand across the cloud and enterprise markets and solutions offered to the networking market.
Overall cloud growth continues to be driven by the shift of both infrastructure and workloads from on-premises to the cloud.

comparisons.peer_summary: Networking offerings include end-to-end InfiniBand and Ethernet platforms with adapters, cables, DPUs, switches, and software, enabling data center-scale computing where the data center, rather than the server, has become the new unit of computing due to large AI and HPC workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both AVGO and NVDA describe the evolution of data center architecture and the role of their offerings in enabling large-scale computing. AVGO highlights that its software solutions allow customers to 'build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale,' emphasizing connectivity and management. NVDA similarly notes a shift in architecture where 'the data center has become the new unit of computing, with networking as an integral part,' supported by 'end-to-end platforms for InfiniBand and Ethernet.' Both recognize the scale and interconnectedness required for modern workloads.

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.

While historically the server was the unit of computing, as AI and HPC workloads have become extremely large spanning thousands of compute nodes, the data center has become the new unit of computing, with networking as an integral part.

comparisons.peer_topic: AI research focus and on-device capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: The company conducts broad research and development across AI, including generative AI, with the goal of advancing core capabilities to run on-device and scaling them across industries, leveraging over a decade of investments focused on power efficiency and personalization.
comparisons.comparison: While AVGO focuses on data center infrastructure software, QCOM focuses on AI research for on-device capabilities. However, both companies discuss the broad scope of AI applications and the goal of scaling these capabilities. AVGO provides software to 'run, manage, connect and protect applications... at scale across... cloud environments.' QCOM conducts research 'to advance AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.' Both address the scaling of AI-driven workloads, albeit in different segments (cloud infrastructure vs. on-device edge/client).

sentences.text: Our infrastructure software solutions offer customers greater choice and flexibility to build, run, manage, connect and protect applications and data at scale across data center and private and hybrid cloud environments.

We conduct broad, leading research and development across AI, including generative AI, from fundamental research to platform and applied research, with the goal of advancing AI core capabilities to run on-device, and scaling them across industries and use cases.
